A1.justification: Both complete 37-page PDFs describe the same BIRCH-Trees benchmark and DINOvTree method. Text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A-D are readable and directly comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original height-estimation and classification experiments on three datasets in Tables 1-3, with ablations and prediction analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1-3 and the ablations and prediction analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the identical shared DINOv3 backbone, task-specific cross-attention heads, prediction procedures, losses, and dynamic loss weighting.

E1.justification: Both versions use Quebec Trees, BCI, and Quebec Plantations for individual-tree height estimation and classification. Dataset, domain, task, and test-scenario coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment in Tables 1-3 and Appendix D. No evaluated baseline, including allometric equations, Mask R-CNN, AnySat, PECore, or DINOv3, is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices A-C retain identical splits, sample counts, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and checkpoint-selection procedures.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3-5.4 and Appendix D retain the same component, loss-weighting, classification-loss, parameter-sharing, backbone, and separate-model analyses, alongside identical bias and confusion-matrix analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard errors over five seeds for comparative and ablation results. Seed selection and aggregation practices for prediction plots and confusion matrices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, rankings, and qualitative findings match, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 reports DINOvTree-B threshold accuracy of 88.29% and F1 of 86.89% in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-18 and their accompanying definitions and mathematical reasoning are identical, including crown buffering, height extraction, losses, dynamic weighting, and evaluation metrics. No proofs or formal assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical benchmark and method contributions, performance claims, and the claim of using 54%-58% of competing methods' parameters.

C2.justification: Interpretations of fine-tuning, parameter efficiency, height bias, and classification errors remain identical. The rare-species limitations in Section 6 and explanations of label uncertainty and intra-genus confusion in Appendix D are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware, and baseline-adaptation details. Project and data-access information is unchanged; the updated arXiv version link adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements elsewhere, and all 83 reference entries are identical. No cited work or relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 24 Mar 2026 to v2 dated 4 Jul 2026. This is an administrative text update; paper prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: All 23 figures and 14 tables retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Body and appendix layouts match; rendered pages 2-37 are pixel-identical, and page 1 differs only in the administrative stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, experimental evidence, mathematical content, and Appendices A-D are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its associated link has no meaningful effect on clarity, reproducibility, evidential support, or overall paper quality.
